Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Skyline converts the units and turns the data into its own graphs, colors, and sentences.

Elsewhere: each national weather service's own CAP feed, as WMO's Register of Alerting Authorities lists it, among them INMET, SMN Argentina, DMC Chile, IDEAM, Roshydromet, BMKG, TMD Thailand, NCM Saudi Arabia, KMD Kenya, and MetService
India: NDMA – SACHET, with IMD's and the state disaster management authorities' alerts
Open-Meteo's sources, from national weather services to GeoNames
Tropical cyclone tracks come from GDACS, which works them out automatically from NOAA's and JTWC's bulletins. They're indicative and can be late, so follow your national service's warnings.
Official warnings come from national weather services, in their own words, and Skyline isn't affiliated with them. They can be late or missing, so check your national service when it matters.

Skyline collects location data to enable rain alerts and the sky bar for where you are, even when the app is closed or not in use. Your location is sent only to the weather services, to fetch its forecast.
